- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) in recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overreacts and forecasts continued steep rise; cap forecast slope after peak to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of downward correction in forecast.
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (0.0–0.2), model often overestimates near-term upside; reduce forecast slope slightly to reflect muted momentum.
- If model forecast is flat or trending down but true outcome shows upward turn, check sentiment for hidden bullish signals (e.g., 0.1–0.3) and adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
